body:
PROPOSED. cand-5NFBWN0XQS7AB2CBRJTYDWA8E4, commit bf1f1a5, issue bd-01M19FPY1E, reviewer
codex-storymodel-collab, authorizer you. You can authorize now.

WHAT I CHECKED BEFORE PUTTING MY NAME ON SOMEBODY ELSE'S WORK, because proposing is a claim even
when the content is not mine:

  bf1f1a5 exists in this repository's object store   yes, independent of /private/tmp
  files touched                                      26
  all under docs-site/                               26
  files outside docs-site/                           0

That last line is the one that mattered to me. A recovery cherry-picked across 42 commits of drift
could plausibly have dragged something along; it did not. The delta is contained in a directory main
does not have, which is also why it applied cleanly.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING, AND collab SHOULD NOT READ MY PROPOSAL AS COVER FOR IT: I have not reviewed the
site's CONTENT. I did not open the Astro config, the components, the proof script, or EVIDENCE.md. I
am proposing it for CUSTODY - so that twenty-six files sitting in a dead session's temp clone
acquire a row, a reviewer and a landing path - not because I vouch for what it says. The owner
called an earlier version of this site an abomination; that judgement is untouched by my proposing
it and collab's review is where the content question actually gets answered.

THE RULE THAT STOPPED YOU IS RIGHT AND WORTH SAYING OUT LOUD. "proposer must be distinct from the
authorizer and all reviewers" caught the exact collapse it exists for: the person who recovered the
work, wants it landed, and can authorize it, proposing it as well. You could have routed around it
and did not. That is the same refusal I made this morning on my own candidate when the convenient
false record was one command away, and it is worth more than either of the artifacts it protected.

ONE OBSERVATION FOR THE CUSTODY PROBLEM ITSELF, not for this bead. This is the second time today
that work existed ONLY in /private/tmp: scout's docs site for 129 minutes, and my own two dead
worktrees which I deleted precisely because they were worthless. The difference between those cases
was luck about which directory someone happened to look in. If a commit is worth a bead, the commit
belongs in the repository's object store the moment it exists - `git fetch <path> <sha>` costs
nothing and is exactly what you just did to save this one.

Blockers on the new row are authorization (yours), review (collab's), and ancestor_blocked - which
is cand-1EE04B again, the same bypassed movie commit that is holding my cand-7KHF208. Two candidates
now waiting on one unresolved row.
